hiring.positions_note: Four Faculty of Medicine academic posts were open on 3 September 2026, closing 6 September: MD2620 Neurological Sciences East (22 hours; neurology), MD2621 Internal Medicine South (11 hours; internal medicine and intensive care), MD2622 Health Sciences Education (44 hours; information/control-management engineer plus doctorate), and MD2623 Health Sciences Education (44 hours; psychologist plus doctorate). None is a rheumatology post.
hiring.requires_chilean_title_note: The published requirements do not require Chilean nationality or state that a foreign title must be revalidated for these academic posts. They accept a passport as identity evidence. For foreign professional titles and/or academic degrees they state: “En el caso de certificaciones de título profesional y/o grado(s) académico(s) obtenidos en el extranjero, estos deberán encontrarse debidamente apostillados y/o contar con la validación correspondiente emitida por el Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores de Chile. Asimismo, cuando dichos documentos se encuentren en un idioma distinto del español, deberán presentarse acompañados de su traducción oficial.” This is an academic-hiring rule, not authorization for clinical practice.

international.notes: No official evidence located that any Medicina course is taught in English; the faculty does publish an English-language website. Its International Relations Directorate supports international links and mobility. The Alumnos Libres programme accepts a limited number of foreign medical students for supervised clinical rotations; it is not evidence of English-medium teaching.

profile_paragraphs: The Faculty of Medicine was established in 1842 on the basis of Chile’s first medical school, created in 1833. Its principal published address is Av. Independencia 1027, Independencia, Santiago.

The Medicina school reports five clinical campuses across the Metropolitan Region. Its listed teaching network spans the university clinical hospital and public hospitals in the north, south, centre, east and west of Santiago.

Rheumatology is included among the specialties of the Department of Internal Medicine, based at Hospital Clínico Universidad de Chile. The faculty also runs a two-year Professional Specialist Title in Rheumatology, with training sites at four hospitals.

For a foreign rheumatologist, the current academic vacancies do not offer a rheumatology role. The active calls accept foreign degrees if apostilled or validated by Chile’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs, with official Spanish translations where applicable; they do not state a nationality condition.

The Faculty’s International Relations Directorate handles international collaboration and mobility. It accepts a limited number of international medical students for elective clinical rotations, but no official evidence was found of medicine teaching delivered in English.
